source: NCERT Class XII, Politics in India Since Independence, Ch. 7 (Regional Aspirations).

sections.heading: 1. Regional Aspirations in a Diverse Nation
points: India's diversity gives rise to **regional aspirations** — demands for autonomy, statehood, or recognition of regional identity.
The Indian approach: **accommodation of diversity within a democratic framework** (rather than suppression).
Regional aspirations are seen as a **normal part of democratic politics**.

sections.heading: 2. Jammu and Kashmir
points: **J&K** had a special status (earlier **Article 370**); a complex history of accession, autonomy demands, and militancy/insurgency.
Internal (regional/religious diversity within the state) and external (Pakistan) dimensions.
A key example of the challenge of accommodating regional aspiration and national integration.

sections.heading: 3. Punjab and the North-East
points: **Punjab** — the **Akali Dal** and demands (Anandpur Sahib Resolution); the crisis of militancy in the 1980s, **Operation Blue Star (1984)**, and the assassination of Indira Gandhi; later restoration of peace (Punjab Accord/Rajiv-Longowal Accord, 1985).

**North-East:** demands for **autonomy, statehood, and against 'outsiders'/migration**; the **Assam Movement (against illegal migration)** → the **Assam Accord (1985)**; **secessionist movements (Nagaland, Mizoram)**; the **Mizo Accord (1986)** brought peace to Mizoram.

sections.heading: 4. Lessons of Accommodation
points: Regional aspirations are best handled by **democratic negotiation, autonomy, and power-sharing** — not force alone.
Many conflicts (Mizoram, Punjab) were resolved through **accords and elections**.
The formation of **new states** (e.g. linguistic/regional) reflects accommodation.
Regionalism, when accommodated, strengthens (not weakens) national unity.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: India accommodates regional aspirations within democracy.
J&K = special status (Article 370); complex accession/autonomy history.
Punjab: Akali Dal, Anandpur Sahib Resolution; Operation Blue Star (1984); Punjab Accord (1985).
Assam Movement → Assam Accord (1985); Mizo Accord (1986) brought peace to Mizoram.
Accommodation (accords, autonomy) resolves regional conflicts.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Operation Blue Star was in 1984** (Golden Temple, Punjab).
The **Assam Accord (1985)** followed the Assam Movement (against illegal migration).
The **Mizo Accord (1986)** brought peace to **Mizoram**.
India's approach to regionalism is **accommodation**, not suppression.
